newsitem.title: FRANCE: SocGen sees 1996 net attrib, EPS well up.
newsitem.headline: SocGen sees 1996 net attrib, EPS well up.

text.p: French bank Societe Generale said on Wednesday it expected net attributable profit and net earnings per share for 1996 to be significantly up on those of 1995.
It said in a statement it would make a provision in the 1996 accounts for the costs of preparing for introduction of the euro single European Union currency in 1999.
"The net attributable result and the net earnings per share should be significantly up on those of 1995," the bank said in a statement. Results will be published on March 12, it added.
The bank also said it expected capital gains on sales in the second half of the year to be on the same scale of those in the first half, when they came to around 600 million francs.
It said banking in France saw a strong seven percent growth in deposits and managed savings and a healthy performance in special savings schemes and life assurance.
International markets activity also progressed strongly, it said, adding the development continued in corporate banking and commercial banking at the international network level.
